03 / RESOURCES

References & useful tools.

A curated collection of papers, lecture notes, books, and online resources related to Hydrodynamics, General Relativity, and Theoretical High-Energy Physics.

Papers & articles ↘ Books ↘ Courses & lectures ↘ Online resources ↘

01 / LITERATURE

Review papers & articles

Lecture notes and research articles that provide useful introductions to relativistic hydrodynamics, gravitational theory, and related developments in theoretical physics.

RELATIVISTIC HYDRODYNAMICS

Lectures on Relativistic Hydrodynamics

Pavel Kovtun's lecture notes on relativistic fluid dynamics, covering conservation laws, hydrodynamic constitutive relations, and the theoretical foundations of fluid behaviour near equilibrium.

Read on arXiv ↗

GENERAL RELATIVITY

Lecture Notes on General Relativity

Matthias Blau's lecture notes on General Relativity spans across a wide range of concepts and applications related to behaviour of matter and fields in non-Euclidean geometries.

Access the notes ↗

FOUNDATIONS & CONCEPTS

Review article on Carroll physics

A closely related resource for exploring Carrollian physics. Consult the article for its precise scope and applications.

Read on arXiv ↗

02 / BOOKSHELF

Books & monographs

Books are valuable for developing a systematic understanding of the mathematical framework and physical principles underlying field theory and high-energy physics.

01 / FUNDAMENTALS

Course of Theoretical Physics Vol.1-10

Landau & Lifshitz

A detailed treatment of fundamentals of physics spanning from mechanics, electrodynamics, quantum mechanics, relativistic QM to theory of elasticity, fluids and statistical physics. Can truely be characterized as old testaments of physics !

Fundamentals
02 / QUANTUM FIELD THEORY

Quantum Field Theory

Mark Srednicki, 2004.

An introductory text to quantum field theory, two out of three parts of which were posted on arXiv. Here is a link to the preprints.

Access the preprint SPIN-ZERO ↗

Access the preprint SPIN-HALF ↗
Quantum fields Symmetry Spin
03 / GENERAL RELATIVITY

General Relativity

Sean Carroll, 1997.

Sean Carroll's lecture notes provide a freely accessible complementary resource for studying spacetime geometry, tensors, and gravitational theory.

Access lecture notes ↗
Geometry Tensor calculus

03 / LEARNING

Courses & lectures

Online courses and recorded lectures offer complementary ways to strengthen mathematical foundations and explore topics beyond the scope of a single textbook.

OPEN COURSEWARE

MIT OpenCourseWare

A collection of freely accessible university course materials. Useful for reviewing fluid mechanics, differential equations, classical mechanics, and related mathematical methods.

Explore courses ↗

VIDEO LECTURES

PIRSA-Perimeter Institute's video library

The Perimeter Institute has a huge collection of recorded video lectures and courses that can be useful for brushing up old concepts or learning entirely new ones across all domains of physics.

Browse lectures ↗

04 / RESEARCH TOOLS

Useful websites

These platforms are useful for discovering research papers, following developments in theoretical physics, and tracing connections between related publications.

01 / PREPRINTS

arXiv

An open-access repository of scientific preprints. Particularly useful for following developments in high-energy physics, nuclear theory, mathematical physics, and general relativity.

02 / LITERATURE DATABASE

INSPIRE-HEP

A literature and bibliographic database for high-energy physics. Useful for finding publications, authors, citation records, and related research in particle physics and theoretical high-energy physics.

05 / NOTES

Using this collection

This is a working collection rather than an exhaustive bibliography. The resources are selected for their relevance to my interests in Hydrodynamics, Field theory, and Theoretical High-Energy Physics.

I intend to expand the list with more specialised review articles, research papers, lecture notes and other resources as I encounter useful material.

Suggestions for additional resources and relevant references are welcome.
